title: BELA Act 4: SGB governance and accountability
description: Conflicts of interest and recusal, paying staff, the HOD's power to step in, and the new budget and financial reporting rules for public school SGBs.

lessons.title: Conflicts of interest: declare and step out
lessons.summary: The new section 26 tells every SGB member exactly when to declare an interest, who counts, and when to leave the room.
lessons.body:
## 🎯 Why this lesson matters

Many SGB scandals start with a contract going to a member's relative while nobody said anything. The BELA Act (Basic Education Laws Amendment Act 32 of 2024) replaced section 26 of the South African Schools Act 84 of 1996 (SASA) with a detailed recusal rule. BELA s20 did this. It applies to governing bodies of **public schools**. If you sit on a board of governors at an independent school, your own constitution and policies govern conflicts, but the same habits are good practice.

## 📢 When you must declare (s26(1))

Before the SGB discusses, or decides on:

- the **recruitment or employment of staff**, or
- the **procurement of goods and services** for the school,

a member must declare to the SGB any direct or indirect personal and financial interest that the member, or any of their family members, close friends or business partners, has. This includes:

1. a personal interest in an entity conducting business with the school, or in a business or commercial or financial activity undertaken by the SGB;
2. a financial or other obligation to an entity conducting business with the school; and
3. a gift, hospitality, sponsorship or other benefit received from an entity conducting business with the school.

### 👨‍👩‍👧 Who counts as "family" (s26(7))

Family member means a parent, sister, brother, child or spouse of the member, and includes a life partner, a relative who lives permanently with the member, and any other relative who is dependent on the member. Note that close friends and business partners are also covered by s26(1), even though they are not "family".

> 💡 Tip: Make "declarations of interest" a standing item at the start of every SGB and committee agenda, and minute each declaration (or "no declarations") by name.

## 🚪 Recusal: leave the room (s26(3) and (4))

A member who has a personal or financial interest must recuse themselves and **withdraw from the meeting** for the whole discussion and decision on that issue. Staying silent in the corner is not enough.

If the SGB knows that a member who is present has a personal interest in a matter, the SGB **may not take a decision** on that matter until the member has withdrawn.

## ✉️ Anyone can raise a flag (s26(2))

Any person may inform the chairperson of the SGB or the principal, in writing, of a possible conflict of interest concerning an SGB member. That could be a parent, a staff member or a supplier who lost a tender.

## 👥 Committees too (s26(6))

Section 26 applies, with the necessary changes, to SGB committees and committee members. Your finance committee, tender or procurement committee and staff selection panels are all covered, including co-opted members.

## ⚖️ Consequences (s26(5))

If a member contravenes s26, the Head of Department (HOD) may, after due process as contemplated in the code of conduct for SGB members:

- suspend the member; or
- terminate their membership.

### 📘 The code of conduct for SGB members

SASA s18A already required every province's MEC to determine a code of conduct for SGB members, which all members must follow and which must include due process for disciplinary proceedings. BELA did not rewrite s18A, but the new s26(5) links to it: the HOD must follow the due process in your province's code before suspending or removing a member. Ask your district office for the current provincial code.

> ⚠️ Watch out: If a tender goes to a member's relative while the member sat in the meeting, the decision may be challenged and the member risks removal.

## 💸 No pay for SGB work (s27(2))

BELA s21 clarified that no SGB member may be remunerated in any way for performing their duties or for attending meetings and school activities.

## ✅ Key points

- Declare any direct or indirect personal and financial interest before the SGB discusses staff recruitment or procurement (s26(1)).
- Family, close friends and business partners all count, and gifts and hospitality must be declared.
- A conflicted member must leave the meeting, and the SGB may not decide until they have (s26(3) and (4)).
- The HOD may suspend or remove a member who breaks s26, after due process under the provincial code (s26(5) and s18A).
- SGB members may not be paid in any way for SGB duties or meetings (s27(2)).

lessons.title: Staff, money and business with the school
lessons.summary: Rules on paying state-employed staff extra, educators doing business with the State, and who may chair the SGB and its finance committee.
lessons.body:
## 💼 Paying state employees extra (SASA s38A)

Many SGBs pay teachers extra for coaching, extra lessons or running the tuck shop. SASA s38A controls this, and BELA s29 tightened it. It applies to public schools.

### The application (s38A(2) and (3))

An SGB may apply to the employer (the provincial education department) for approval to pay a state employee any remuneration, or to give a state employee any other financial benefit or benefit in kind. The application must be in writing, lodged at the employer's office, and must state:

1. full details of the nature and extent of the remuneration or benefit;
2. the reasons for it;
3. if practicable, its monetary value;
4. the process that will be followed and the resources that will be used to pay the employee; and
5. the extent of compliance with SASA s20(5) to (9) (the SGB's rules on employing staff).

### The employer's duty (s38A(6))

The employer may not unreasonably refuse the application.

### Show it in the budget (s38A(8))

The remuneration or benefit must be reflected in the school budget presented to the general meeting of parents under s38(2), with a monetary value where practicable.

> 💡 Tip: "Benefits in kind" include things like free accommodation on the school grounds or private use of a school vehicle. If it has value and goes to a state employee, treat it as covered by s38A and get approval.

### Draft regulations (not final yet)

BELA s39 allowed the Minister to make regulations on the prohibition of unauthorised remuneration and benefits (SASA s61(1)(aC)). On 7 August 2026 the Department of Basic Education published draft regulations on this for comment, closing on 5 September 2026. The DBE said the drafts make clear such payments may not be made informally or without oversight. As at October 2026 we have not seen final regulations, so check with your district office before relying on them.

## 🚫 Educators may not do business with the State (EEA s19)

BELA s49 inserted s19 into the Employment of Educators Act 76 of 1998 (EEA). An educator may not:

- conduct business with the State; or
- be a director of a public or private company conducting business with the State.

A contravention is an offence (a fine, imprisonment of up to five years, or both) and serious misconduct. If an educator is found guilty of it in a disciplinary process, the employer must terminate their employment.

> ⚠️ Watch out: The Act does not spell out whether a contract with a public school counts as business with the State. If a teacher's company quotes to supply your school, stop and ask your district office how the department applies s19 before you proceed. If the teacher is also on the SGB, s26 (Lesson 1) applies as well.

## 🪑 Who may chair (s29(2))

BELA s23 substituted s29(2):

- Only a parent member who is **not employed at the school** may serve as chairperson of the SGB (s29(2)(a)).
- **Where reasonably practicable**, only a parent member who is not employed at the school may chair the **finance committee** (s29(2)(b)). This is new.

## 🧒 Learner members and staff appointments (s32(4))

BELA s24 added s32(4): a learner member of the SGB may not take part in meetings where recommendations for staff appointments are decided, may not sit on interview panels, and may not be involved in staff appointments in any other way. BELA also replaced the word "minor" with "learner" in s32(1) to (3).

## 📦 Central buying of learning materials (s21(3A))

BELA s14 inserted s21(3A): the HOD may, in consultation with the SGB, centrally procure identified learning and teaching support material. An SGB may still buy from a supplier if that is more cost effective, but it must give the HOD documentary proof that it is.

## ✅ Key points

- Any extra pay or benefit in kind to a state employee needs a written s38A application and approval, and must appear in the budget with a value where practicable.
- Draft s38A regulations were published in August 2026; confirm whether they are final before relying on them.
- Educators may not do business with the State or direct companies that do (EEA s19, inserted by BELA s49).
- Only a non-employed parent may chair the SGB, and where practicable the finance committee (s29(2)).
- Learner members may not be involved in staff appointments (s32(4)).

lessons.title: When the HOD steps in
lessons.summary: The HOD's powers to withdraw SGB functions or dissolve an SGB, the steps the HOD must follow, and the new dispute procedure.
lessons.body:
## 🧭 Three levels of intervention

BELA rewrote what the Head of Department (HOD) may do when a public school SGB is not performing. Think of a ladder:

1. a dispute, handled through the new dispute procedure (s59A);
2. withdrawal of one or more functions (s22);
3. dissolution of the whole SGB (s25).

## ✂️ Withdrawal of functions (s22)

BELA s15 substituted SASA s22.

### The power (s22(1))

The HOD may, on reasonable grounds, withdraw one or more functions of an SGB, for example its financial functions.

### The process (s22(2))

Before acting, the HOD must:

1. inform the SGB in writing of the intention and the reasons;
2. give the SGB a reasonable opportunity to make representations;
3. give due consideration to those representations; and
4. inform the SGB of the final decision in writing.

In urgent cases the HOD may act first, but must immediately afterwards give written reasons, allow representations, consider them and give a written final decision (s22(3)). The HOD may reverse or suspend the action for sufficient reasons (s22(4)).

### Who does the work (s22(5) to (8))

The HOD must appoint sufficiently qualified persons to perform the withdrawn functions for up to three months. The HOD may extend this by further periods of up to three months each, but the total may not exceed one year. These persons must build the SGB's capacity so that it can perform the functions again, and they have exclusive voting rights and decision-making powers on the functions they were appointed for.

### Appeal (s22(9))

Any person aggrieved by the HOD's decision may appeal to the MEC, who must communicate a decision with written reasons within 30 days of receiving the appeal.

## 🧨 Dissolution (s25)

BELA s19 substituted SASA s25.

- **The power (s25(1)):** the HOD may, on reasonable grounds, dissolve an SGB that has ceased to perform its functions under SASA or provincial law.
- **The process (s25(5)):** the same four steps as for withdrawal: written notice with reasons, a reasonable opportunity for representations, due consideration, and a written final decision.
- **Interim persons (s25(2) to (4)):** the HOD must appoint sufficiently qualified persons to perform all the SGB's functions for up to three months, extendable in periods of up to three months to a maximum of one year. They have exclusive voting and decision-making powers.
- **New election (s25(6)):** the HOD must make sure a new SGB is elected within a year after appointing those persons.
- **Appeal (s25(7)):** an aggrieved person may appeal to the MEC, who must decide, with written reasons, within 14 days of receiving the appeal.

> ⚠️ Watch out: The appeal periods differ. The MEC has 30 days to decide a withdrawal appeal under s22(9), but 14 days for a dissolution appeal under s25(7). Check which section the HOD's letter relies on.

## 🤝 The new dispute procedure (s59A)

BELA s37 inserted s59A for disputes between the HOD and an SGB:

1. The parties must try to resolve the dispute informally.
2. If that fails, the aggrieved party gives written notice describing the issues and a proposed resolution.
3. If the dispute is not resolved within 14 days of the notice, each party nominates a representative within seven days, and the representatives meet within 14 days of nomination.
4. If it is still not resolved, the SGB may appeal to the MEC, who must decide within 30 days and inform the SGB in writing.

A similar procedure, without the MEC appeal step, applies to disputes between the MEC and an SGB (s59A(2)). Section 59A does not apply where SASA already provides an appeal, such as admission appeals or appeals under s22 and s25 (s59A(3)).

> 💡 Tip: If the department writes about poor performance, reply in writing and diarise every deadline.

## ✅ Key points

- The HOD may, on reasonable grounds, withdraw one or more SGB functions (s22) or dissolve an SGB that has ceased to perform (s25).
- Except in urgent withdrawal cases, the HOD must give written notice, hear representations, consider them and decide in writing first.
- Appointed persons serve up to three months at a time, to a maximum of one year, and a dissolved SGB must be re-elected within a year.
- MEC appeals: 30 days to decide under s22(9), 14 days under s25(7).
- Other HOD and SGB disputes follow the step-by-step procedure in s59A.

lessons.title: Budgets, school fund and financial reporting
lessons.summary: New budget transparency rules, the 10 per cent deviation rule, loans and leases, annual statements and quarterly reports to the HOD.
lessons.body:
## 💡 Why this matters

BELA tightened how public school SGBs plan, change and report on money. (Subsidised independent schools have separate rules under SASA s48, not covered here.)

## 📊 The budget meeting (s38(3))

SASA s38(2) already required the SGB to present its budget to a general meeting of parents for approval. BELA s28 substituted s38(3). When notice of that meeting is given:

- the budget, together with a document explaining it, must be made available to parents through the school's existing communication channels; and
- parents must be told that the document and budget will be available for inspection at the school at least 14 days before the meeting.

## 🔁 Changing the budget mid-year (s38(4) and (5))

If the SGB needs to:

- deviate from the approved budget by **10 per cent or more** of the initial budget; or
- reallocate funds to a purpose different from what parents approved,

it must present the deviation or reallocation to a general meeting of parents convened specifically for that purpose, on at least 14 days' notice, for approval by a majority of parents present and voting. An explanatory document with reasons must be shared through the school's channels, and parents must be told it will be available for inspection at least 14 days before the meeting.

### Quorum (s38(6) and (7))

A quorum of **10 per cent of parents** is required for both the budget meeting and a deviation meeting. If the quorum is not reached, the chairperson sets a second meeting and notifies parents 14 days before it; the principal must hand every learner a copy of the notice at least seven days before; and **no quorum** is required at the second meeting.

> ⚠️ Watch out: Moving sports money to fix the roof is a reallocation under s38(4)(b), even if the total is unchanged.

## 🏦 Loans, leases and overdrafts (s36)

BELA s26 amended s36:

- **s36(2):** an SGB may not enter into any loan, lease or overdraft agreement **for any purpose** without the written approval of the HOD. Before BELA, approval came from the MEC.
- **s36(4)(a)(i):** leasing the school's immovable property needs approval, but approval is not required for a lease of 12 months or less.
- **s60(4)(b),** amended by BELA s38: the State is not liable for damage or loss if s36(2) was not complied with.

## 🏧 The school fund (s37(1))

BELA s27 changed one word: the SGB must establish a school fund and administer it in accordance with **directives** issued by the HOD. Ask your district for the current provincial directives.

## 📒 Records and annual statements (s42)

BELA s31 substituted s42. The SGB must:

1. keep records of all investments, donations and funds received and spent, and of assets, liabilities and financial transactions;
2. draw up annual financial statements as soon as practicable, and not later than **three months** after the end of each financial year, in line with the MEC's guidelines;
3. present the financial records and statements to a general meeting of parents; and
4. tell parents they will be available for inspection at the school at least 14 days before that meeting.

## 📮 Reports to the HOD (s43(5))

BELA s32 requires the SGB to submit to the HOD:

- within **30 days after the end of each quarter**, a quarterly report on all income and expenditure, in the format the HOD directs; and
- within **six months** after the end of each financial year, the annual financial statements, audited or examined under s43.

## 🔍 Investigations (s43(4))

On just cause shown, the HOD may authorise officers to investigate the school's finances, ask the Auditor-General to audit, or appoint forensic investigators. Before BELA this power sat with the MEC.

> 💡 Tip: Build a finance calendar: quarterly report dates, the three-month and six-month deadlines, and the budget meeting.

## ✅ Key points

- Share the budget and an explanatory document, and make them available 14 days before the parents' meeting (s38(3)).
- A deviation of 10 per cent or more, or any reallocation, needs a special parents' meeting (s38(4)); quorum is 10 per cent, with no quorum at a second meeting (s38(6) and (7)).
- Any loan, lease or overdraft needs the HOD's written approval (s36(2)).
- Annual statements within three months, presented to parents (s42); quarterly reports within 30 days and statements to the HOD within six months (s43(5)).
- The HOD may order investigations, Auditor-General audits or forensic investigations (s43(4)).

questions.text: Before the SGB discusses which supplier will repaint the school, what must a member whose brother owns a bidding company do?

options.text: Declare the interest and withdraw from the meeting for the discussion and decision
Declare the interest but stay and abstain from the vote
Nothing, because only spouses count as family members under s26
Ask the principal to vote on their behalf

questions.explanation: SASA s26(1) and (3), substituted by BELA s20, require a declaration of any direct or indirect interest before procurement is discussed, and recusal and withdrawal from the meeting. A brother is a family member under s26(7).

questions.text: Who may inform the SGB chairperson or principal in writing of a possible conflict of interest of an SGB member?

options.text: Only another SGB member
Only the HOD
Any person
Only a parent of a learner at the school

questions.explanation: SASA s26(2), substituted by BELA s20, says any person may in writing inform the chairperson or the principal of a possible conflict of interest concerning a governing body member.

questions.text: What may the HOD do if an SGB member breaks the recusal rules in section 26?

options.text: Fine the member up to 12 months' school fees
Suspend or terminate the member's membership, after due process under the SGB code of conduct
Dissolve the whole SGB immediately
Nothing; only the parents can remove a member

questions.explanation: SASA s26(5), substituted by BELA s20, allows the HOD, after due process as contemplated in the code of conduct for SGB members (determined under s18A), to suspend or terminate the member's membership.

questions.text: The SGB wants to give a teacher free use of a school house for coaching the first team. What does SASA s38A require?

options.text: Nothing, because a benefit in kind is not remuneration
Only a resolution of the SGB
Approval by the learner representative council
A written application to the employer for approval, and the benefit shown in the budget with a value where practicable

questions.explanation: SASA s38A(2), (3) and (8), as amended by BELA s29, cover remuneration, other financial benefits and benefits in kind. They require a written application to the employer and reflection in the budget presented to parents.

questions.text: Under the new section 19 of the Employment of Educators Act, what is an educator prohibited from doing?

options.text: Conducting business with the State or being a director of a company that does
Doing any paid work outside school hours
Serving on the SGB of their own school
Owning shares in any listed company

questions.explanation: EEA s19, inserted by BELA s49, prohibits an educator from conducting business with the State or being a director of a public or private company conducting business with the State. It is an offence and serious misconduct.

questions.text: Who may chair the finance committee of a public school, where reasonably practicable?

options.text: The principal
Any educator member of the SGB
Only a parent member of the SGB who is not employed at the school
The school's bursar

questions.explanation: SASA s29(2)(b), substituted by BELA s23, says that where reasonably practicable only a parent member who is not employed at the school may chair the finance committee.

questions.text: Before the HOD dissolves an SGB that has ceased to perform its functions, which step is required?

options.text: A court order confirming the dissolution
Written notice of the intention and reasons, and a reasonable opportunity for the SGB to make representations
A vote of 10 per cent of parents
Approval by the Minister

questions.explanation: SASA s25(5), substituted by BELA s19, requires the HOD to inform the SGB in writing with reasons, allow representations, consider them, and give a written final decision before dissolving the SGB.

questions.text: Persons appointed by the HOD to perform withdrawn SGB functions may serve for a maximum total period of:

options.text: Three months, with no extension
Six months
Until the next regular SGB election, however long
One year

questions.explanation: SASA s22(5) and (6), substituted by BELA s15, allow an appointment of up to three months, extendable in further periods of up to three months each, but the total may not exceed one year.

questions.text: Halfway through the year the SGB wants to move money from the sports budget to the maintenance budget. What does SASA s38(4) require?

options.text: Approval at a general meeting of parents called for that purpose, on at least 14 days' notice
Nothing, as long as the total budget stays the same
Only the finance committee's approval
Only the HOD's written approval

questions.explanation: SASA s38(4)(b), added by BELA s28, requires any reallocation of funds to a different purpose, and any deviation of 10 per cent or more, to be approved by a majority of parents present and voting at a meeting called on at least 14 days' notice.

questions.text: By when must an SGB send the HOD its quarterly report on income and expenditure?

options.text: Within 14 days after the end of each quarter
Within 30 days after the end of each quarter
Within three months after the end of each quarter
Only once a year, with the annual financial statements

questions.explanation: SASA s43(5)(a), substituted by BELA s32, requires a quarterly report on all income and expenditure to reach the HOD within 30 days after the end of each quarter, in line with the HOD's directives.
